teaching.hint: When a third type appears, which early trees can no longer belong to the current valid collection?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A legal collection is a contiguous range containing at most two fruit types. As the right endpoint moves, removing a prefix can restore validity without losing any longer valid range ending there.
solution_outline.approach: Sweep the right endpoint through the array while maintaining type counts in the current range. Whenever a third type appears, move the left endpoint right until only two types remain; record the largest valid length.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: After each right-endpoint step, the maintained range contains at most two types, and its left endpoint is the earliest one that makes this endpoint valid. Type counts describe exactly the range's contents.
solution_outline.correctness: Every possible collection has an endpoint. For each endpoint, the maintained earliest valid left boundary gives the longest legal collection ending there: any earlier start has too many types, while any later start is shorter. Taking the maximum over endpoints therefore finds the global optimum.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time because each boundary advances at most n times; O(1) auxiliary space because the type map holds at most three types during repair.
solution_outline.pitfall: A basket can hold unlimited fruit of one type; treating it as a capacity of one fruit changes the problem.

accepted_alternatives: Track each type's last index in the current range instead of its count, removing a type when its final occurrence passes the left boundary.
common_wrong_turns: Choose a noncontiguous set of trees
Reset the entire range on seeing a third type
Shrink only one position when several old fruits remain
source_fidelity_notes: The farm story was shortened while keeping the rightward consecutive-picking rule, two unlimited single-type baskets, value bounds, and maximum-length objective.
